name: ECW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The top belt of the diary's ECW. Its own title history opens on Shane Douglas's second reign, won in March 1994 and running when the game world leaves real events in July 1994, and the shows of the first ten are set inside Raven's reign that ran from 23 November 2005 to 26 September 2006; Raven is the billed champion at Wrestlepalooza, where he keeps it over Goldberg. Raven keeps the belt through the pages of July, August and September 2006: he retains at Summer Assylum when Shawn Michaels interferes against Paul Burchill, and at Heatwave he sides with Charlie Pag and Paul Burchill and keeps it over Goliath with their help. Raven's reign ends at Anarchy Rulz on 26 September 2006 by the diary's title history, when Shawn Michaels superkicks him in a five-on-five brawl and pins him; Michaels loses the belt back to Raven at Guilty As Charged, in the Triangle Match with Rob Van Dam, after Stephanie Mcintosh lowblows him. At Masters Of Pain on 29 December 2006 by the diary's title history Sabu takes the belt from Raven with a Triple Jump Moonsault after Zakk Wylde punches the champion; Sabu keeps it over Cactus Jack at Got Blood? and is still champion when the pages of February 2007 end. At Living Dangerously Sabu keeps the belt over Steve Austin and Raven then hits him with an Evenflow DDT; the next night on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven beats Sabu for it with Paul Burchill's and Goliath's help (the diary's own history prints Sabu's reign as ending, and Raven's sixth as starting, on "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the change is filed at month precision), and keeps it over Shane Douglas at Baptism Of Fire on 29 March 2007 with CM Punk's interference; Raven is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end, with Paul Burchill, who won the Baptism Of Fire match, due a title shot at Hardcore Heaven. At Cyberslam Raven keeps the belt over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match when Paul Burchill, the special referee, counts fast and calls a submission Rhino never gave, after which Burchill turns on Raven with a C-4 (on the next Blood, Sweat and Beers Burchill and Shane Douglas, the masked man, tell how the plan ran for seven months); at Hardcore Heaven, in a match that is not for the title, Raven beats Burchill after CM Punk threatens to throw Kelly Thomaselli off the stage, so that Burchill may never challenge for the belt; Raven's sixth reign continues in the diary's history and is still going when the pages of June 2007's second week end, with Owen Hart booked to challenge him at Wrestlepalooza and Bret Hart in a Triangle Match for the belt. At Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 Raven keeps the belt in the elimination Triangle Match with Bret and Owen Hart, then is Chokeslammed by the mystery signing, Mark Calaway; on Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman forces Raven into a non-title match against Vito Thomaselli, and Calaway's Chokeslam lets Vito pin the champion. At Summer Assylum (Friday, week 4, July 2007) Raven keeps the belt over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway; Raven is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with the history's date for the reign's end, 1 October 2007, still ahead. At Heatwave in August 2007 Vito Thomaselli beats Raven in the Barbed Wire Cage Match and is presented with the belt, but on the next Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven reads out a clause of the contract that voids any title change after outside interference, and says the belt is still his; Rhino wins the first Buck Stops Here Match at Heatwave and is booked against Raven at Anarchy Rulz, with the history's date for the reign's end, 1 October 2007, still ahead. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Raven beats Rhino with Mark Calaway's help and is then chokeslammed by Calaway; on the first Revolution of October Owen Hart makes him tap to the Sharpshooter after Chris Jericho's chair shot and is the champion (1 October). Owen retires after Guilty As Charged, where Chris Jericho wins the Ultimate Submission Match on a ruling that his tap came after the time limit and loses the belt minutes later when Raven, using the Commissioner's right to book one match of his choosing at a pay-per-view, pins him with a Raven Effect (26 October); the company's owner then strips Raven of his powers as Commissioner and books Paul Burchill against him for November To Remember XV. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as the champion and that Paul Burchill will beat him at November To Remember; on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers he makes the match a Loser Leaves ECW Match, with anyone outside it who touches either man to be fired, and says that the man who stays will be the Undisputed ECW World Heavyweight Champion. Raven is still the champion when the diary's preview of the card ends. Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill at November To Remember XV (30 November 2007 in the history) and leaves ECW; Burchill is the new champion and, on the Saturday show, defends under the Code of Diminishing Extremes' modified British rules (twelve five-minute rounds, two falls out of three); CM Punk, now the leader of Raven's Nest, loses to him in a non-title match, and Rhino, who gores Burchill twice and beats Vito Thomaselli in a number one contendership match, is booked against him at Masters of Pain.

name: ECW World Television Championship
epitaph: The belt Chris Jericho carries through the diary's first ten shows, in a reign that its own title history dates from 23 November 2005 to 8 August 2006. He keeps it over Lance Storm, Doug Williams, Bryan Danielson and Cactus Jack, and again on the tenth show, where the commentary counts his reign as entering its seventh month. Chris Jericho keeps the belt through the pages of July, then loses it to Rhino on 8 August 2006 by the diary's title history, wins it back a week later, and loses it again to Rhino in the Triangle Match with Christian at Heatwave. Rhino keeps the belt until Anarchy Rulz, where the returning Shane Douglas beats him for it; Kensuke Sasaki takes it from Douglas at Guilty As Charged and still holds it when the pages of November 2006 end. Vito Thomaselli takes the belt from Kensuke Sasaki on the debut Blood, Sweat and Beers on 4 December 2006 by the diary's title history, when Francine lowblows Sasaki; Vito keeps it through December and January with Francine's help and then the New Age Enterprise's, until Bret Hart beats him for it with the Sharpshooter on Blood, Sweat and Beers on 6 February 2007; Bret Hart is champion when the pages of February 2007 end. Paul Burchill takes the belt from Bret Hart at Living Dangerously on 28 February 2007 by the diary's title history, with a clean C-4 after he sends the New Age Enterprise away, and loses it back to Bret Hart on Blood, Sweat and Beers on 22 March 2007 when his knee gives way; Bret Hart loses it to Chris Jericho in the Triangle Match with Christian on Blood, Sweat and Beers on 15 April 2007, and Jericho is champion when the pages of April 2007 end, with Rob Van Dam booked to challenge him at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam on 24 April 2007 by the diary's title history Rob Van Dam takes the belt from Chris Jericho in the Lumberjack Match, when Shawn Michaels Superkicks Jericho off the ropes while Christian is held at ringside and a Five Star Frog Splash wins; at Hardcore Heaven on 29 May 2007 AJ Styles, who debuted in May, takes it from Van Dam with the Canadian Connection's hockey sticks and a Styles Clash while Michaels is away from ringside; Styles is champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end, having beaten Rey Mysterio Jr. with a low blow and lost a non-title match to Juventud Guerrera. On Revolution in June 2007 AJ Styles beats Juventud Guerrera with a low blow and the Styles Clash, and at Wrestlepalooza he keeps the belt over Guerrera with another Styles Clash after pushing Guerrera's foot off the rope while the referee does not see it; at Summer Assylum he keeps it a third time when Francine's pretended turn lets Guerrera hit Styles with a low blow and Christopher Daniels hits Guerrera with the belt; Styles is champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Guerrera's challenge for Heatwave still unanswered and Ultimo Dragon billed against him on the next Revolution, so the history's 28 September 2007 end is still ahead. At Heatwave in August 2007 AJ Styles keeps the belt in the Stairway To Hell Match, in which Juventud Guerrera, challenging with his mask at stake, loses the mask; in September Styles beats Jerry Lynn on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and Ultimo Dragon is booked against him at Anarchy Rulz, so the history's 28 September 2007 end is still ahead. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Ultimo Dragon pins AJ Styles with an Asai DDT after Francine's interference (28 September); at Guilty As Charged AJ Styles wins the four-way Stairway To Hell Match by pulling the belt from the strap above the ring (26 October), and Juventud Guerrera storms in with a chair. In November 2007 Styles keeps the belt over Juventud Guerrera on Blood, Sweat and Beers when the referee misses Guerrera's foot on the rope, and over Rey Mysterio Jr. on Revolution, and loses it on Revolution on the last Monday of the month (26 November) when Guerrera rolls through his Spiral Tap into a pin, for his first title in ECW. Paul Heyman has announced a newly designed belt and a title match at November To Remember XV against the winner of a three-way match, Ultimo Dragon, who is hurt in it (an EMT says 'a cracked sternum'); in a backstage scene the company's owner and Heyman ask Rey Mysterio Jr. to wear Dragon's mask and compete as Ultimo Dragon (PDF pp.1654-1655), and the history lists Guerrera as the champion, 'present'. Juventud Guerrera keeps the belt at November To Remember XV over Ultimo Dragon, whom Francine's lowblow and DDT leave open to a 450 Splash, over The Great Sasuke on the Saturday show and over Eddie Guerrero on Revolution on the first Monday of December; Christopher Daniels is booked against him next, and the history lists Guerrera as the champion, 'present'.

name: ECW World Tag Team Championship
aka: Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships
epitaph: The pair of belts the Dudley Boys hold in the diary's first ten shows, in a reign its own title history dates from 23 May 2006 to 2 August 2006. They beat the Hardy Boys for them on the first show and again on the eighth, and the ring announcer bills both as title matches. The Hardy Boys win the belts in the opening match of the first July post, with Brock Lesnar's help, and the Dudley Boys win them back for what the commentary calls their tenth reign; after Heatwave Raven and Paul Burchill take them, and Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova take them from Raven and Burchill. The Blue World Order keep the belts through the autumn, beating Burchill and Abyss at Anarchy Rulz, until Abyss and Goliath, as Monsters Inc., take them from the bWo at Guilty As Charged. The Whole F**kin' Show, Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels, take the belts from Monsters Inc. at November To Remember on 26 November 2006 by the diary's title history, keep them against Monsters Inc. at Got Blood? and on Revolution in February, and are still champions when the pages of February 2007 end. The Iron Saints, Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli, take the belts from the Whole F**kin' Show at Living Dangerously on 28 February 2007 by the diary's title history, with a Spike Powerbomb on Shawn Michaels after Rob Van Dam steps off the apron, and lose them at Baptism Of Fire on 29 March 2007 in the first Halflife Handicap match, when Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels win with a Five Star Frog Splash on Salvatore; the Whole F**kin' Show are champions when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam the Whole F**kin' Show keep the belts over Los Increibles in the Ladder Match when Rob Van Dam pulls them down; at Hardcore Heaven they keep them over the Canadian Connection, who won the three-way dance for the number one contendership at Cyberslam, when Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone while Rob Van Dam runs to help Traci, pins Christian with a third Sweet Chin Music; the champions quarrel through June but are still champions when the pages of June 2007's second week end. At Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 the Whole F**kin' Show keep the belts over the Hardcore Innovators with simultaneous covers; the Dudley Boyz, returned to ECW, win the number one contendership, and at Summer Assylum the champions beat them in the Tables Match with Shawn Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table; they are still champions when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with the history's 26 October 2007 date for the reign's end still ahead. After Heatwave in August 2007 the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new holders of the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, the Hardcore Innovators; in September they keep the belts over the Dudley Boyz on Revolution, and the Innovators ask for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz, with the history's 26 October 2007 date for the reign's end still ahead. At Guilty As Charged in October 2007 the Dudley Boyz win the Ladders, Chairs, Canes and Flaming Tables Three Way Dance from the Whole F**kin' Show, whose partners fall out when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes down Rob Van Dam, and from the Hardcore Innovators; the history lists the Dudley Boyz's reign, their ninth, from 26 October to 4 November 2007. In November 2007 the Innovators still carry all four belts to the ring; Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match at November To Remember XV in which the Dudley Boyz and the Hardcore Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills that match with the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (30 November 2007 in the history) the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles, the belts the diary calls the first unified ones; on Revolution on the first Monday of December the titles change hands in a restarted Three Way Dance: Slyk Tayshaun Dudley and Big Dick Dudley Jr. win them when Slyk makes Bubba Ray tap to the Boston Crabs, and they keep them over Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08 on the Saturday show. The history lists the Second Generation of Dudleyz as the champions from 4 November 2007, a date that the text does not agree with: the order of the shows is the text's, the dates are the history's.

name: ECW International All Action Championship
epitaph: A belt exclusive to Revolution, announced on the first Revolution of August 2006 for a month-long tournament of fast-paced wrestlers; Jushin Lyger, Ultimo Dragon, Yoshihiro Tajiri and Psicosis are the names the commentary gives for it. Tajiri beats Lyger in the final at Heatwave to become the first champion and keeps the belt over Super Dragon on Revolution after Heatwave. Tajiri keeps the belt until Anarchy Rulz, where Jushin Lyger wins the Triangle Match with AJ Styles and him; The Great Sasuke takes it from Lyger at Guilty As Charged and loses it to Vito on F' The Mainstream a week later, and Vito keeps it over Chris Daniels on Revolution. Vito loses the belt to Christopher Daniels at November To Remember in the Stairway To Hell Match with Super Crazy, when Daniels hangs on to the harness as the ladder collapses and drops to the floor with the belt; Daniels keeps it over Michael Shane at Got Blood? and is still champion when the pages of February 2007 end. The diary's own title history omits Daniels's reign and lists Vito as champion until 28 February 2007, so the history and the text of the shows disagree; both are recorded, and the reign dates follow the text. At Living Dangerously on 28 February 2007, the date the history gives for CM Punk's win, Punk takes the belt from Christopher Daniels in the Triangle Match with Michael Shane when Raven hits Daniels with a chair, so on that date the history and the text of the shows agree even though the history leaves Daniels out; Punk pins Daniels again with a low blow on Blood, Sweat and Beers and is champion when the pages of April 2007 end, with Lance Storm, who won an International All Action title shot in the Stairway To Hell match at Baptism Of Fire, set to challenge him at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam CM Punk keeps the belt over Lance Storm in the No Way Out Match with a GTS while the masked man traps Abyss and Vito outside, and at Hardcore Heaven he keeps it over Storm again with a GTS after Monsters Inc chokeslam Storm onto Abyss's knee; Punk is champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June 2007 CM Punk knocks out Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas with the belt, and at Wrestlepalooza and Summer Assylum Vito Thomaselli turns on him and powerbombs him through a table; the belt is not defended in the range, and Punk is champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with the history's 29 September 2007 end still ahead. At Heatwave in August 2007 CM Punk hits Paul Burchill with the belt and Vito Thomaselli with a GTS; in September he defends the belt for the first time in months, keeping it over Lance Storm, Big Sasuke Cool and Eddie Guerrero, and Vito Thomaselli is booked against him at Anarchy Rulz, with the history's 29 September 2007 end still ahead. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Vito Thomaselli pins CM Punk with a Crucifix Roll-Up (29 September in the history); at Guilty As Charged CM Punk wins the Last Man Standing Match when referee Jim Molineaux stops it, with Monsters Inc. at ringside (26 October), and he keeps the belt over Lance Storm on Blood, Sweat and Beers. On the first Revolution of November 2007 Paul Heyman has about fifteen security guards strip Punk of the belt ('it ain't yours anymore', 3 November in the history) and starts the International All Action Title Tournament, open to 'hard working, respectful talent'. The first-round winners are Ricky Marvin (over Kensuke Sasaki), Teddy Hart (over Psicosis), Slyk Tayshaun Dudley (over Scorpio Sky) and Excalibur (over Paul London); in the semi-finals Slyk beats Teddy Hart and Ricky Marvin beats Excalibur, and the final, Ricky Marvin against Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, is on the card of November To Remember XV. Ricky Marvin beats Slyk Tayshaun Dudley in the final at November To Remember XV (30 November 2007 in the history) after Big Dick Jr. interferes against his own cousin, and is the new champion; the Code of Diminishing Extremes sets the title to lucha libre rules, with a twenty count and two falls out of three.

name: ECW Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The Dudley Boyz's own belt, which they declare on Blood, Sweat and Beers the night after Summer Assylum in July 2007, when the Dudley family bring out the old World Tag Team Championships, "back from when Bubba and I were dominating anything that stood in our path", and D-Von says they are rechristened the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, because Paul Heyman will not give them a fair crack at the Whole F**kin' Show's belts; the diary's own title history (PDF p.8, 'ECW/Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship') does list it, dating the Dudley Boyz's first reign from 28 July 2007. The Dudley Boyz make their first defence on Revolution in August 2007, beating the bWo with a 3D on Hollywood Nova after Chessman and Oz hit the bWo with the belts, and beat Balls & Axl, who beat the Samoan Gangstas to earn the match, with a 3D on Axl on Blood, Sweat and Beers; the Hardcore Innovators challenge for them at Heatwave on 24 August 2007 and Los Guerreros are billed as third challengers, so the Dudleyz are still the holders when the pages of August 2007's first week end. At Heatwave in August 2007 the Hardcore Innovators, Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer, win the belts from the Dudley Boyz in the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match, the Dudleyz having defended them earlier that month against Los Guerreros, the Samoan Gangstas and the Briscoe Boys; Joey Styles says the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship has become the ECW Hardcore Championship, and the diary's later posts call the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, 'newly rechristened'. The Innovators ask the holders of the World Tag Team Championship for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz and are still the holders when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Guilty As Charged in October 2007 the Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance for the tag titles and take the Dudleyville belts back from the Hardcore Innovators (26 October); the Innovators leave the arena with all four belts anyway, and the history lists the Dudleyville belt's unification with the World Tag Team Championship on 30 November 2007, still ahead. In November 2007 the Innovators still carry the Dudleyville belts with the others; Paul Heyman announces that they are to be unified with the World Tag Team Championship at November To Remember XV. At November To Remember XV the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators, and the Dudleyville belts are unified with the World Tag Team Championship on 30 November 2007, the date the history gives.

name: ECW Lioness Championship
epitaph: The first Lioness Championship, crowned at Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 in a Lioness' Den Match between Jazz, Kelly Thomaselli and Alexis Laree: Alexis Laree wins by rolling up Kelly Thomaselli and hooking her tights, and the diary's own title history lists her as the champion, 'present'. She keeps the belt on Revolution and Blood, Sweat and Beers over Daizy Dudley, Beulah McGillicutty, Traci and Mika Akino, and at Guilty As Charged over Jazz when a new member of Raven's Nest, Nattie Neidhart, runs in and the two of them hit a Double DDT; she is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 she and Nathalie lose a Lioness Pack Match to Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli, and on the last Revolution before November To Remember XV she pins Jazz in a non-title match after Nathalie hits Jazz with the belt; Kelly Thomaselli challenges her for the title, and the diary's preview of the card bills Kelly Thomaselli against Alexis, the champion. At November To Remember XV Alexis beats Kelly Thomaselli in the Lioness match with Nathalie's belt shot, and on Revolution and the Saturday show of the first week of December over Mika Akino; Kong, back 'from APW' with Prince Nana, flattens her with a Sit-out Powerbomb, and the diary's next preview books Kong and Akino against Alexis and Nathalie.
